newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen mixed at open, await data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen mixed at open, await data.

text.p: Wall Street is expected to open mixed Wednesday, with initial stock and bond market direction dependent on durable goods figures.
Barring a big surprise in the economic data, stocks will ultimately move slightly higher, adding to Tuesday's gains and focusing again on technology stocks, analysts said.
Stocks will watch bonds' reaction to durable goods orders for April, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Orders are forecast to show a rise of 1.3 percent, following a decline of 2.6 percent in March.

A strong number could spark interest rate concerns and derail bonds and stocks at the market open, analysts said. A weak number might allay rate fears, lowering yields on bonds and boosting share prices, they said.

"The big event today is the durable goods data, which have the potential to show a restoration of the solid demand which caused the Fed to tighten in March," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics. "Or they could prove that an economic slowdown has taken on some durability."
But other analysts say the data will receive less long-term attention because it is known to be volatile.
On Tuesday stocks shrugged off weakness in bonds, which rose above a key seven percent yield on inflation concerns sparked by a surge in U.S. consumer confidence in May.

A buying spree in technology shares sent U.S. stock prices to record high closing levels. The Dow industrials finished up 37.50 points at 7383.41, while the Nasdaq composite added 19.49 points to 1409.21.
Early Wednesday the Standard & Poor's futures index was off 3.55 points at 847.80.
The long bond was off 3/32 to yield 7.04 percent, compared with yesterday's 7.03 percent close.

Technology stocks were expected to be active again today, particularly International Business Machines Corp, which will trade on a post-split basis, said James Cramer, president of Cramer Berkowitz & Co.
"The techs will be the focus again today," he said. "We could see them come in a bit from yesterday...but I don't see any big retracement."
Tokyo's 225-share Nikkei average rose 461.45 points, or 2.32 percent, to 20,351.34.
In London the FTSE 100 was off 6.1 points at 4675.5. U.S. stocks were mixed in thin trading in London.
